source.title: Variational principles in grid generation and geometric modelling: theoretical justifications and open problems

accepted.question_text: In a two-dimensional harmonic-coordinate grid-generation setting, a map x(u) is first obtained by minimizing the Dirichlet energy (1/2) integral tr((grad x)^T grad x) du under first-kind boundary conditions, and the useful computational grid is the inverse map u(x). After exchanging dependent and independent variables, the inverse map is governed by the nonlinear functional (1/2) integral over x(Omega) of tr((grad u)^T grad u)/det(grad u) dx. Does an existence theorem hold for this inverse-map functional, and under what precise conditions is an extremal of this functional actually the inverse of the harmonic map x(u)?

For the quasi-isometric variational principle whose feasible condition is det grad y > t Phi(det grad y, grad y) almost everywhere with t>0, for which broad classes of boundary data and solutions can one prove global uniqueness of the minimizer and convergence of finite-element approximations, beyond the smooth near-identity regime where an implicit-function-theorem argument is expected to apply?
accepted.context_brief: Finite-element convergence for quasi-isometric variational maps

accepted.question_text: For the same quasi-isometric functional, can one characterize stability conditions for minimizers and prove, if true, that every minimizer remains strictly inside the feasible set, meaning that there is a positive margin epsilon and a parameter t1>t+epsilon such that det grad y - t1 Phi(det grad y, grad y) > 0 almost everywhere? Such a result would support the weak Euler-Lagrange formulation and possible higher regularity of grad y.
accepted.context_brief: Stability and strict feasibility of quasi-isometric minimizers

accepted.question_text: In mapping theory, can every locally invertible mapping of interest, including a quasi-isometric mapping, be approximated by a sequence of locally invertible piecewise-affine mappings that converges to it? Here quasi-isometric means that local metric distortion is uniformly controlled, for example by bounded singular values or by a condition of the form det grad y > t Phi(det grad y, grad y).

Given a mapping whose total metric distortion is below a threshold 1/t in the quasi-isometric condition det grad y > t Phi(det grad y, grad y), can one construct a convergent sequence of piecewise-affine approximations such that every approximation also stays below the same distortion threshold 1/t, and can this construction be made practical?

For surface grid generation, how can a discrete variational principle be made invariant under the choice of surface parameterization, including non-smooth parameterizations, and what discrete analogue of the finite-element patch test should replace the usual finite-element patch-test condition for spatial mappings?

Can the quasi-isometric variational functional be formulated directly on manifolds equipped with polyhedral metrics, with extrema sought among bounded-curvature mappings, and can proportional convergence of such polyhedral metrics to a metric satisfying a tangent-cone condition be used to prove convergence of both functional values and weak gradients or Euler-Lagrange formulations?
accepted.context_brief: Polyhedral-metric formulation of variational mapping problems

accepted.question_text: When a suitable polyhedral metric is available for the variational grid problem, is it mathematically or computationally necessary to realize that metric by an actual polyhedron, or is it enough to run numerical simulation and minimization directly on manifolds with polyhedral metrics?
accepted.context_brief: Need for realizing polyhedral metrics as polyhedra

accepted.question_text: Does every compact two-dimensional manifold of bounded curvature without peak points admit a finite quasi-isometric chart, meaning finitely many disk-like domains with quasi-isometric flattenings, quasi-isometric coordinate changes on overlaps, and union equal to the whole manifold?
accepted.context_brief: Finite quasi-isometric charts for bounded-curvature manifolds

accepted.question_text: For quasi-isometric parameterization of a manifold by cut-and-paste flattening, how should one choose an optimal finite set of cuts, for example cuts that reduce pocket depth and enable either global flattening with unfolding or flattening of polygons cut from the manifold?

Given a surface tessellation that approximates geometry to a prescribed chordal error but induces a very poor polyhedral metric, how can one compute a quasi-isometric flattening of the resulting extremely ill-conditioned triangulation so that the surface can be remeshed with nearly equilateral triangles and convergence-preserving patch-test behavior?

Direct fetching of the zbMATH page returned a Cloudflare challenge. The zbMATH REST API identified record 5077468 as V. A. Garanzha, Numerical Linear Algebra with Applications 11(5-6):535-563 (2004), DOI 10.1002/nla.363.

Exact-title recovery found the ResearchGate full-text page. Its visible title, DOI, author, journal, year, and page range match the zbMATH record, and the body contains the article text. A direct ResearchGate PDF download was attempted but the local shell could not resolve the host, so the HTML full-text page was used as the primary source artifact.
